description: The Sin Archbishops is a group of second-year high school students consisting of three programmers (with experience in languages such as C++, C#, GML and Java), an artist (specialized in draw, research, game design and development) and a musician.
summary: Disasteronomy is a 2D pixel-art, co-op space-disaster game (LAN multiplayer with push-to-talk voice chat) built in Godot 4 with C#. It turns real spaceflight risks into playable teamwork. In Level 1, an astronaut on a spacewalk (EVA) must climb handrail by handrail across a spacecraft in zero gravity, using a SAFER-style jet pack and a tether that can snap, to reach a frozen cryogenic propulsion stage and calibrate its stuck actuators before time runs out. In Level 2, the crew re-enters the Deep Space Habitat: communication with CAPCOM drops, smoke fills the ship and the team must split up to restore the life-support (ECLSS) valves and regulate the oxygen while avoiding electric hazards. As sanity falls, players begin to hallucinate. [CHALLENGE: one sentence on how the game addresses the challenge you chose.] It matters because it makes EVA procedures, isolation stress and crew coordination understandable and memorable for a general audience.
details:
What it does: Disasteronomy is a co-op 2D game where players face cascading failures during a space mission. Phase 1 (EVA / Vacuum Calibration) uses inertia-based movement, one-handrail-at-a-time climbing, a tether that breaks after repeated extreme swings, limited SAFER jet charges and a spin-the-mouse calibration minigame on a cryogenic propulsion stage. Phase 2 (Deep Space Habitat) is a side-view maze filled with smoke, electric hazards and crates; players restore three ECLSS valves (hold-to-turn) and then regulate the oxygen at the central module while managing a sanity meter that causes hallucinations when it drops.

How it works: Godot 4.7 (Mono/C#, .NET 8) with an ENet host-authoritative multiplayer layer (GDScript autoload) with LAN room discovery and push-to-talk voice chat. Scenes are driven by small manager scripts (lobby terminal, Phase 1, Phase 2) and a shared progress state.

Benefits and impact: it teaches, through play, why handholds, tethers, life-support systems and crew communication matter, and how isolation and stress affect decision making. It can be used for outreach and education about human spaceflight.

Tools: Godot, C#, GDScript, Aseprite for pixel art, Git. AI-assisted development is disclosed in the SI section.

Q Creativity: pixel-art horror-lite tone, physical grip-by-grip climbing, sanity-driven hallucinations and split-the-team objectives.

Factors considered: accessibility of controls, short play sessions (about 10 minutes), co-op communication by voice, and keeping all assets credited and license-checked.
